title: Microbatch congestion probing and soft-fairness backpressure
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement and evaluate a congestion-probing microbatch admission controller that enforces soft-fairness across priority classes and applies KV-cache-aware memory reclamation to avoid OOMs at high QPS. The feature uses lightweight probes to detect transient congestion and adjusts per-priority microbatch thresholds using an AIMD-inspired controller. We will also add an age-based KV compaction heuristic and staggered KV eviction to minimize decode stalls when reclaiming GPU memory.
acceptance_criteria: Controller runs behind a feature flag and can be toggled per-cluster
End-to-end load tests show p99 latency increase <= 5% at 2x baseline QPS compared to current stable, while reducing OOM events to zero in synthetic mem-pressure scenarios
Per-priority tail-latency fairness metric improves (ratio of p99 of low-priority to high-priority drops by >= 30%)
KV cache compaction reduces peak GPU memory by >= 12% under long-tail token workloads without increasing average token compute > 3%
Monitoring surfaced: admission_threshold, probe_success_rate, aimd_state, kv_eviction_rate, stall_duration, and rollout timeline documented
Integration tests and a canary rollout plan exist with automatic rollback on regressions
tasks: Design: write spec for congestion probe signals and AIMD parameterization (latency targets, increase/decrease factors)
Runtime: implement per-priority microbatch threshold state machine behind FF
KV: implement age-score compaction and staggered eviction window
Instrumentation: add metrics and traces for admission decisions and KV eviction events
Load testing: build JMeter/locust scenario for mixed-priority long-tail traffic
Rollout: feature flag canary (10% -> 40% -> 100%), automated rollback on p99 > threshold or OOMs
Documentation: update runtime tuning docs and add runbook for backpressure incidents
